measurement: native invocation attempt for the newly covered accessibility controls
result: NOT EXERCISED NATIVELY. On the initial surface only task-search was present; it exposes ValuePattern and not InvokePattern, which is expected for a text field, so the invoke threw. surface-switcher, flow-search, compare-change-a, compare-close, stop-request and stop-reconcile were absent because they belong to other surfaces, and reaching those needs navigation this session cannot deliver. The change is therefore verified by the unit tests and the Gate only, not by a native activation.
what_this_means: Adding the listener is justified by the preview-button evidence - the same defect class, fixed and measured - but for these eight controls the fix is unmeasured. No claim is made that they now respond to accessibility activation.
guard_limitation: What the tests actually establish: a count over the production half of the file, proven to fail when a production listener is renamed away, and a per-control pass that finds each control's id and requires an explicit listener before the next .id(" occurrence. That boundary is not an element boundary - compare-close's window spans about seventeen thousand characters and reaches flow-node click handling, and surface-switcher is a group whose children carry their own listeners - so the per-control pass shows the handlers exist in production code, not that each control is bound to its own listener. An element-scoped binding test is not done.
exclusions: Five click targets remain: the flow node list (lib.rs:3498), the flow edge list (lib.rs:3574), candidate cards (lib.rs:4266), task rows (lib.rs:4456) and the flow diagram nodes (lib.rs:5424). Each would need per-target design of how the captured values (click keys, entity handles, indices) are carried into an accessibility activation and what that activation should mean, so they were left out of this pass rather than migrated blind. This is not a claim that a plain Click action cannot express them - surface-switcher captures index and item and was migrated successfully - only that the mapping has to be decided per target. flow-diagram-region is a real element but not a click target, so it is in neither list.
guard_fix: FIXED AND PROVEN, IN TWO PARTS. The count-based test now reads only the production half of the file (before the first #[cfg(test)] module) so its own literals cannot satisfy it, and renaming one production listener makes it fail. A second test checks each of the eight controls individually by locating its .id(...) and requiring an explicit listener within the following text, because a count cannot show that a particular control has one. Structural analysis of every .on_click remains undone.
